questions.subtopic: Insider Threat Active Exfiltration — First Action
questions.question: What is the FIRST action?
questions.scenario_context: A financial advisory firm (clients managing $14B in assets) receives an EDR + DLP alert at 3:38 PM Friday: senior portfolio manager (employed 11 years, resignation letter submitted Monday with 2-week notice, last day next Friday) has copied 4,200 client-portfolio files (~18GB) to a personal cloud storage account over the past 90 minutes; current rate of transfer is ~200MB/minute. The DLP alert correlates: client files contain non-public investment strategies, client contact lists, fee schedules. The portfolio manager is currently logged in at the office. The Chief Compliance Officer, CISO, and General Counsel are reachable on a conference bridge.

options.A: Open a multi-track coordination call: CCO + CISO + GC + HR + executive comms + IT to align on the response framework before taking technical action.
options.B: Confront the portfolio manager directly in their office to ask about the file transfers and obtain their explanation before initiating any technical containment actions.
options.C: Notify the affected clients of potential exposure of their portfolio data and engage external forensics before taking action on the portfolio manager's access.
options.D: REVOKE access IMMEDIATELY through IdP (disable AD account + revoke OAuth tokens + force-disconnect cloud sessions) — every minute extends exfiltration and fiduciary exposure; revocation completes in 60 seconds.

questions.key_concept: Insider exfiltration in progress FIRST action = revoke access immediately. Coordination, interview, notification all follow. Single surgical action because every minute extends exfiltration scope and fiduciary exposure.
questions.pre_read: For time-critical insider-exfiltration questions, anchor on REVOKE ACCESS FIRST. The exfiltration-rate clock dominates other considerations.
questions.correct_explanation: When EDR + DLP correlate to confirm active insider exfiltration with a known user identity and active session, the FIRST action is IMMEDIATE ACCESS REVOCATION. Rationale: (1) EVERY MINUTE EXTENDS EXFILTRATION SCOPE — at 200MB/minute, 10 minutes of coordination = 2GB additional client data exfiltrated; (2) DETECTION-TO-ACTION GAP IS WHERE ADVERSARIES OPERATE — the user is currently logged in and aware (or will become aware) that they have a narrow window; revocation closes the window; (3) REVOCATION IS FAST — IdP-managed AD disable + OAuth token revocation + force-disconnect of cloud sessions completes in 60 seconds; faster than any coordination call; (4) FIDUCIARY OBLIGATION — financial advisory firm has fiduciary duty to clients; allowing continued exfiltration while coordinating is a breach of that duty; (5) FORENSIC PRESERVATION — endpoint must be preserved for forensic imaging (NOT wiped), but ACCESS REVOCATION doesn't affect the endpoint; it prevents continued network exfiltration. After revocation: (a) preserve endpoint for forensic imaging (do not wipe; do not return to circulation); (b) IR call with CCO + CISO + GC + HR; (c) interview with legal counsel present (employment law + criminal referral considerations); (d) client notification per fiduciary duty and SEC/FINRA reporting obligations; (e) regulator notification (SEC Regulation S-P breach + state breach laws as applicable); (f) post-incident review of monitoring gaps that allowed 90 minutes of exfiltration before detection. The pattern is CONTAIN-FIRST: stop the bleeding, then diagnose, then communicate.

wrong_explanations.A: Multi-track coordination call is appropriate AFTER access revocation. The 200MB/minute transfer rate means every minute of coordination is ~200MB of additional exfiltrated client data. Revocation is critical-path; coordination follows.
wrong_explanations.B: Direct confrontation before access revocation tips off the user that exfiltration is detected, potentially accelerating exfiltration (forced copy to USB before access is revoked), and gives the user opportunity to delete evidence on their endpoint. Revoke first; interview second.
wrong_explanations.C: Client notification before access revocation continues to allow exfiltration during notification preparation. Notification is a downstream step after the exfiltration is stopped; engaging external forensics is appropriate but is also downstream of stopping the active exfiltration.

tips: Trap is A — for INSIDER THREAT specifically, 'multi-track coordination call' is uniquely seductive because the scenario invokes HR + legal + comms + IT as required pre-action stakeholders; but with a measurable 200MB/minute transfer rate, every coordination minute is more client data exfiltrated and a fiduciary-duty breach. REVOKE FIRST, coordinate second.

Active insider exfiltration = revoke access first (AD disable + OAuth revoke + session force-disconnect). Coordination, interview, notification all follow. Containment dominates communication in time-critical exfiltration scenarios.

Exam-day shortcut: when stem describes ACTIVE INSIDER EXFILTRATION WITH MEASURABLE RATE AND KNOWN IDENTITY, look for IMMEDIATE ACCESS REVOCATION; coordination-call, confront-user, and notify-clients-first framings each fail the exfiltration-rate-clock test.
